points: 1 Identity and release: Command A is a 111B-parameter decoder-only enterprise model covering 23 languages, with Command R7B as a smaller sibling; weights are released under CC-BY-NC (non-commercial) with an acceptable-use addendum (p. 1-2).
2 Architecture: SwiGLU, GQA, sliding-window attention (RoPE) and full attention (NoPE) interleaved 3:1, parallel transformer block, shared input/output embeddings, no bias terms (p. 3).

3 Pre-training recipe: JAX on H100s with FP8 matmuls over FP32 master weights and a BF16 phase; cooldown anneals the learning rate linearly from 2.5e-4 to 1e-6 over 50,000 steps while context grows from 8k (30,000 steps) to 32k, 128k and 256k (10,000, 5,000, 5,000 steps) (p. 4-5).

4 Post-training pipeline: Instruct model, then six SFT experts (Code, Safety, RAG, Math, Multilingual, General Long-Context), SFT Soup, six RL experts, RL Soup, then polishing (best-of-N SFT, then offline SRPO and online CoPG alternated); SRPO is a min-max self-refinement preference objective and CoPG a KL-regularised reward objective (p. 5-7, 17).

5 Merging: linear weight averaging with weights found by manual and brute-force search, informed by 500 evaluation metrics; SLERP and task vectors gave no significant improvement; 1.8% average drop versus the best expert, most metrics within 2.5%, code least preserved (p. 16, 34).

6 Withheld: layer count and widths, vocabulary and window size, pre-training token count (only 'trillions'), data-mixture proportions, merge weights, compute, and nearly all Command R7B specifics; appendices with hyperparameters are not in the main text.
7 Efficiency: serving footprint of two A100s or H100s; up to 156 tokens/sec, stated as 1.75x GPT-4o and 2.4x DeepSeek V3 (p. 1); KV cache 75% of Llama 3.3 70B's at 8k and 32.9% at 128k (p. 34).

8 Academic and agentic results with baselines: MMLU 85.5 vs GPT-4o 89.2 (Table 3; 85.7 in Table 1), DeepSeek V3 88.5, Llama 3.3 70B 86.0; MATH 80.0 vs Llama 3.3 70B 77.0, DeepSeek V3 70.2, GPT-4o 68.5; Taubench Retail P@1 60.0 vs GPT-4o 60.6 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet 69.2; BFCL 63.8 vs GPT-4o 72.1.

9 Human evaluation and polishing: about 800 internal prompts; Command A win rate vs GPT-4o is 50.4 / 51.4 / 46.8 on general / reasoning / code; polishing raised it from 43.2, 41.4 and 30.0 for the pre-polish merge (p. 37).

10 Enterprise benchmarks (internal): generative pass rate over 22 tasks 94.2% vs Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 84.2 and GPT-4o 79.1; RAG correctness 4.73 vs Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 4.72; answerable / unanswerable accuracy 96 / 91 (p. 32-34).
